rapport_notes: Amy is friendly, patient with the customer's technical interruptions, and responsive to concerns; tone remains warm throughout.
process_discipline_notes: Amy asked 'Does that make sense so far?' after the full estimate but did not hold silence—she immediately continued with email confirmation without waiting for a substantive response.

evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: No time-boxed ask or promise of accurate quote framing present. Amy launches directly into logistics questions after a brief greeting.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Asked after extensive probing: 'Do you have any specific concerns or what are you most worried about for this upcoming, anything at all?' — this comes after detailed inventory questions, storage details, and drive-time framing.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer said 'Nope, not at all' to the agenda question, so no concerns were raised. No follow-up opportunity existed. Per the N/A exception in item #3, this receives full credit.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Partial anchor given: 'three and a half to four hours depending on traffic' for drive time, but no framing of typical crew size × hours for the full load/unload (e.g., 'a typical move this size with two movers takes 6–8 hours').
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass_line_estimate_is_window: 'However, your for the for Monday, your current address, or the storage address is a bit outside of our free service zone, so there's a $75 travel fee' and later 'since we're hourly based basically for each day, you only pay for the actual time to use and then the one time travel fee, one time, overnight fee, no more, no less.'
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass_line_beats_it_pay_less: 'since we're hourly based if possible, that's a possibility that we can load drive and unload on the same day' and 'basically for each day, you only pay for the actual time to use.'
evidence_quotes.close_missing: No rate-lock language ('your rate locks when you book'). No explicit ask ('would you like our help with your move?'). Customer initiates the close by asking to call back or receive the email; Amy complies without a closing pitch.

top_strength: Amy handled a complex two-day estimate with multiple fee components clearly and patiently, and she remained warm and responsive to the customer's traffic concerns and clarification requests.
coaching_note: Begin every call with a time-boxed quid pro quo (e.g., 'This should take about 6 minutes, and I'll get you an accurate quote in return'), ask the agenda question before any logistics probing, and always hold silence after 'Does that feel fair?'—never re-pitch immediately or hand off without the customer's active response.
